messages.text: I'm getting "emulation error: insufficient funds, swap bounced" when building a USDT→TON swap transaction via Omniston SDK. The user has USDT in their wallet. What could cause this and how do I debug it?

text_entities.text: I'm getting "emulation error: insufficient funds, swap bounced" when building a USDT→TON swap transaction via Omniston SDK. The user has USDT in their wallet. What could cause this and how do I debug it?

messages.text:
Summary of findings and likely fixes for “emulation error: insufficient funds, swap bounced” on TON via Omniston:

Root causes (most common first)
• No TON for gas: The wallet has USDT (jetton) but 0 TON, so the jetton transfer/swap message can’t pay fees and bounces.
• Jetton wallet not deployed: The user’s USDT jetton wallet contract may be undeployed; first outbound transfer requires a bit of TON to deploy/init.
• Too little attached TON in message: The swap/jetton transfer to the router needs a sufficient forward_ton_amount/forward_value to cover processing and response. If it’s too low, the internal message bounces.
• Misconfigured params: Missing/incorrect response_destination or send_gas_to, wrong network (testnet/mainnet), or outdated SDK/build.
• Emulation context/state: Emulator uses on-chain state; if it sees zero TON or undeployed jetton wallet, it will return “insufficient funds” even before broadcast.

What to do (practical checklist)
• Ensure TON dust: Fund the wallet with a small TON buffer (e.g., 0.05–0.2 TON). This alone fixes most cases.
• Deploy/initialize jetton wallet: If undeployed, send a tiny TON-funded jetton action (or use SDK helper like getOrCreateJettonWallet) to deploy.
• Raise forward_ton_amount: When sending jetton transfer to the swap router/resolver, attach enough TON (commonly 0.03–0.1 TON) so the router can process and send the result message.
• Verify addresses/params: Correct token master and router addresses, set response_destination and send_gas_to properly, and confirm you’re on the intended network.
• Rerun emulation and inspect phases: Look at action phase/bounce details and exit codes; “insufficient funds” in action phase typically points to fee/forward value issues.
• Update SDK and re-estimate fees: Make sure you’re on the latest Omniston SDK and re-run fee estimation before building the message.
• Don’t rely on gasless for the initial TON message: Even with gasless settlement, the initiating wallet typically still needs TON to send the first internal message unless you’re using a relayer flow.

If you share the emulation payload, the wallet address, and your forward_ton_amount settings, I can pinpoint which of these is biting you.

messages.text: I'm building TonSense Yield — a yield comparator that shows APY across TON, Ethereum, Base and BNB Chain, with one-click swaps via Omniston. What do you think about this product idea? Any suggestions to make it more useful for TON newcomers?

text_entities.text: I'm building TonSense Yield — a yield comparator that shows APY across TON, Ethereum, Base and BNB Chain, with one-click swaps via Omniston. What do you think about this product idea? Any suggestions to make it more useful for TON newcomers?

text: I genuinely like the concept — cross-chain yield comparison with execution in one flow is a real pain point. But there are a few traps I'd watch for, especially with TON newcomers in mind.

Right now, if someone holds USDT on TON and sees "4.1% APY" on a pool, they have no idea whether that's good or bad without manually checking Aave, Compound, Venus, etc. A comparator that does this in real time solves an actual problem.
•

The gap between "I see a better yield" and "I've moved my money" is where most users drop off. If Omniston actually makes that seamless, that's the killer feature.
•

Most TON-native tools only show TON yields. Showing Base or Ethereum yields next to TON gives newcomers context — "oh, I'm earning 4% here but could earn 7% there" is a much more powerful hook than "4% APY" in isolation.

text.text: 1. Yield numbers lie if you don't contextualize them

text:
A flat APY comparison is misleading. 12% on Venus BNB is not the same as 4.1% on TON:

• Is it variable or fixed? (most are variable)
• What's the TVL? (low TVL = higher yield but higher risk of depegs)
• Is the protocol audited? (TON DeFi is early — most pools aren't)
• What are the hidden costs? (bridge fees, gas, slippage)
Show yield
. If someone bridges 1,000 USDT from TON to Base for 7% APY, but the bridge costs 0.5% and gas is $2, their
is more like 1-2%. That's the number that matters for decision-making.

text.text: 2. TON newcomers don't think in chains

text: Your target user probably doesn't know what Base is. They have USDT on TON because someone sent it to them on Telegram. They don't have MetaMask, they don't have ETH for gas on Base, and they definitely don't know what a bridge is.
Abstract the chain entirely. Instead of:

text.text: 🔵 TON: 4.1% APY | 🔴 Ethereum: 3.8% APY | 🔵 Base: 7.2% APY

text: Show:

text.text: Best yield: 7.2% on Base — you'd earn ~$6/month more than your current TON pool. Move in one tap → [Swap & Deposit]

text: And only reveal the chain details on a secondary screen for power users.

text.text: 3. The "one-click" promise is hard to keep

text: From our earlier debugging — the user needs TON for gas, the jetton wallet might not be deployed, cross-chain swaps take minutes to hours, and the destination chain needs gas too. "One click" can quickly become "5 steps, 3 error messages, and a 20-minute wait."
Be brutally honest about the flow. Show a progress tracker:

text.text:
⏳ Step 1/3 — Swapping USDT on TON → Base (~2 min)
⏳ Step 2/3 — Bridging to Base (~5 min)  
⏳ Step 3/3 — Depositing into Aave Base (~1 min)

text: And pre-flight the wallet: check for TON gas, jetton wallet deployment, and destination chain setup
the user clicks "start." If something's missing, say "You need 0.1 TON for gas — here's how to get it" rather than letting them hit an error mid-flow.
Yield comparison without risk context is dangerous, especially for newcomers. Someone sees 15% APY on a BNB pool and goes all-in without understanding they could lose principal.
Add a simple risk tier:

text.text:
Tier      | Label                               | Criteria               
----------+-------------------------------------+------------------------
🟢 Low    | Audited, 6+ months live, TVL > $50M | Aave, Compound         
🟡 Medium | Audited, newer, TVL $5-50M          | Venus, newer TON pools 
🔴 High   | Unaudited, <3 months, low TVL       | Most TON DeFi right now

text: Let users filter by risk. Default to showing only 🟢 and 🟡.
A yield comparator is a one-time tool unless you give people a reason to come back.
Add yield alerts. "Your TON USDT pool dropped from 4.1% to 2.8% — Base is now 2x better. Want to move?" This turns a utility into a habit.
